program_name: Biology of Extreme Environments (BIOEXTREME) — Master's Degree Programme (Corso di Laurea Magistrale). The Didactic Regulation states both official names explicitly: "Master's Degree Program name in Italian: Biologia degli Ambienti Estremi / Master's Degree Program name in English: Biology of Extreme Environments". The English name is the operative one on all University of Naples Federico II international-facing pages. Casing varies across official unina.it pages: the orientamento.unina.it course card renders it "Biology of extreme environments" (lowercase), while the Department of Biology, the Scuola Politecnica e delle Scienze di Base and the Didactic Regulation use "Biology of Extreme Environments". Internal University course code: D53 (www.corsi.unina.it/D53). The programme is commonly abbreviated BExE or BIOEXTREME on Department notices.
teaching_language:
English — the programme is taught entirely in English and is listed in the University of Naples Federico II "International Course Catalogue" (international.unina.it). The orientamento.unina.it course card shows "Language ENG". This is a STANDALONE English-taught degree, not an English track of an Italian-language programme: the Didactic Regulation records "Teaching language: English" for the whole degree, and Art. 4 confirms "The course is taught in English". Both curricula ("Biological Resources" and "Astrobiology") are delivered in English; there is no parallel Italian-language curriculum. Course delivery is "conventional" (in-presence); the FAQ states "Lectures will be in presence and not offered online."

Italian language proficiency is NOT an admission requirement. Italian appears only inside the study plan as an optional/complementary item: both curricula reserve 6 credits in Year II for "Other activity / Italian language * (*for international student)". The University-wide UniversItaly brochure confirms the B2 Italian requirement applies only "For programmes taught in Italian".
campus:
Monte Sant'Angelo — Complesso Universitario di Monte Sant'Angelo, Naples. The orientamento.unina.it course card gives the site as "University of Naples Federico II 'Monte Sant'Angelo Campus, Via Vicinale Cupa Cintia, 26, 80126 Naples (NA)", with "Department of Biology: Building 7". The Department of Biology programme page gives the coordinator's address as "Complesso Universitario di Monte S. Angelo, Università degli Studi di Napoli Federico II, Via Cinthia – 80126 Naples, Italy, Department of Biology – Building 7, Room number: 1D/09". The programme FAQ confirms teaching location: "All classes will be held at the Monte Sant'Angelo Campus, in Naples".

The programme belongs to the Department of Biology (Dipartimento di Biologia) and sits under the Scuola Politecnica e delle Scienze di Base (School of Polytechnic and Basic Sciences). Note the two street-name renderings used across official pages — "Via Vicinale Cupa Cintia, 26" and "Via Cinthia" — refer to the same Monte Sant'Angelo complex; only the internal building/office reference differs.
degree_class: LM-6 (Biologia / Biology). Confirmed identically by three official sources: the orientamento.unina.it course card ("Degree class LM-6"), the Didactic Regulation 2025/26 ("the Master's Degree Program in 'Biology of Extreme Environments' (class LM-6 - Biology)"), and the file naming of the Italian regulation ("Regolamento-Didattico-LM-6-_BExE-Ita_2025-26.pdf"). Duration 2 years, 120 CFU/ECTS. Required entry qualification per the orientamento card: "Degree required Laurea I Livello" (first-level/bachelor degree). Faculty/School: Politecnica e delle Scienze di Base; Department: Biologia.
admission_type:
OPEN ACCESS — the orientamento.unina.it course card states "Admission Libero" (free/open access). There is NO numero programmato, NO capped intake, NO competitive ranking list (graduatoria) and NO rectoral admission call (bando di concorso) for this programme. Art. 5 of the Didactic Regulation leaves any planning of enrolments to the CCD ("The CCD of the Master's Degree Program normally regulates the admission criteria and the possible planning of enrolments except in the case subject to different provisions of law"), and no such cap has been published.

However, "open access" does NOT mean automatic entry. A mandatory two-step procedure applies, and step 1 is a genuine screening gate:

(1) ADMISSION — compulsory for ALL applicants regardless of nationality (Italian, EU and Extra-EU). The candidate submits an online application (Google Form at https://forms.gle/6DNRdeKQ4m5FQEkUA) with all documents merged into a SINGLE PDF, plus the signed "FORM 1 – Recognition of Foreign University Title". The Program Admission Committee evaluates the bachelor degree and transcripts against the curricular requirements and verifies English proficiency. On a positive outcome the Programme Coordinator issues a PRE-ACCEPTANCE LETTER, which is required for enrolment and for the visa application. Art. 5 of the Didactic Regulation makes this compulsory: "Verification of personal preparation is mandatory in any case, and only students in possession of the curricular requirements can access it."
  - EXCEPTION for EU/Italian applicants holding a bachelor in class L-13, L-32 or L-2 (or the D.M. 509/99 equivalents): they "may proceed directly to the Enrollment procedure" without prior evaluation. Applicants with any other bachelor must first e-mail their documents to bioextreme@unina.it for academic evaluation and obtain the Pre-Acceptance Letter.
  - Note: the same Department page and the orientamento card also present the ADMISSION step (Google Form + Form 1) as "common to ALL the students (Italian, EU and Extra-EU)", which sits in tension with the direct-enrolment shortcut granted to L-13/L-32/L-2 holders; see uncertainty_notes.

(2) ENROLMENT — route depends on citizenship/residency:
  - Italian and EU students: online via SegrePass (https://www.segrepass1.unina.it/Welcome.do).
  - Extra-EU students resident abroad: mandatory pre-enrolment on the Universitaly portal (https://www.universitaly.it/) uploading the Pre-Acceptance Letter, then visa, then final enrolment (matriculation) in Naples at the Student Office.

No SAT, no TOLC, no CEnT, no national test, no motivation-letter requirement, no GPA threshold, no interview for the general case (an English interview may be required — see entry_exam_or_test).
academic_requirements:
Master-level entry: a three-year first-cycle university degree (Laurea Triennale / bachelor, minimum 3 years) or an equivalent qualification obtained abroad deemed suitable by the Course Council.

A) DIRECT CURRICULAR ELIGIBILITY (Art. 4, Didactic Regulation 2025/26) — holders of an Italian three-year degree in:
  - class L-13 (Scienze Biologiche / Biological Sciences)
  - class L-32 (Scienze e Tecnologie per l'Ambiente e la Natura / Sciences and Technologies for the Environment and Nature)
  - class L-2 (Biotecnologie / Biotechnologies)
  - or the corresponding classes under the former Ministerial Decree 509/99.

B) GRADUATES OF OTHER CLASSES — must evidence an adequate number of CFU per scientific-disciplinary sector (SSD). Art. 4 of the Didactic Regulation and the orientamento.unina.it card state: "at least 30 CFU BIO/*, MED/04, MED/42, 6 CFU between MAT/01-MAT/09, ING-INF/05, INF/01, 6 CFU between FIS/01-FIS/08, 6 CFU between CHIM/01-CHIM/04, CHIM/06, CHIM/12."
  The Scuola Politecnica e delle Scienze di Base page restates this as: at least 30 ECTS in the Biological Science area (BIO/*, MED/04, MED/42); at least 6 ECTS across the Mathematical and Computer Sciences area (MAT/01–MAT/09), Industrial and Information Engineering (ING-INF/05, INF/01) and Physical Sciences (FIS/01–FIS/08); at least 6 ECTS in the Chemical Sciences area (CHIM/01–CHIM/04, CHIM/06, CHIM/12).

C) [uncertain] A THIRD, STRICTER TABLE appears in the official programme FAQ ("LM BExE – faq-1 Admission and Enrollment", last update May 15, published May 2026) for "Students with a different Bachelor degree": the bachelor must be at least 90 CFU, and the applicant must hold at least 60 CFU distributed as — MAT/01–MAT/09: 6 CFU; FIS/01–FIS/08: 6 CFU; CHIM/01, CHIM/03, CHIM/06, CHIM/12: 12 CFU; BIO/09, MED/04, MED/42: 6 CFU; BIO/01, BIO/02, BIO/03, BIO/05, BIO/06, BIO/07, BIO/16, BIO/17: 20 CFU; BIO/04, BIO/10, BIO/11, BIO/12, BIO/13, BIO/18, BIO/19, AGR/07, MED/03, MED/07: 20 CFU; plus "at least 30 CFU of Biology". This FAQ table is materially heavier than Art. 4 of the Didactic Regulation (60 CFU total vs 30+6+6+6 = 48 CFU) and the two are not reconciled on any unina.it page. The Didactic Regulation is the binding instrument.

D) SUBJECT-KNOWLEDGE EXPECTATION — the Department page states: "For the admission to the Master Degree in BIOEXTREME, students are required to have knowledge in basic fields, such as biology and microbiology; ecology; general, organic and inorganic chemistry; biochemistry." The Department's plain-English summary of the entry rule is: "A Bachelor (min 3 years) in Biology, Biotechnology or Natural Sciences or equivalent degree / Alternatively a minimum of 30 CFU in biological related subjects / Alternative careers will be evaluated on a case by case basis from the admission commission."

E) FOREIGN QUALIFICATIONS — Art. 4: "For graduates from foreign universities, the adequacy of the curricular requirements is assessed case by case on the basis of the coherence between the programs carried out in the different disciplinary areas, the training bases deemed necessary for the advanced training offered by the course of study, as well as the knowledge linguistics." The qualification must additionally be documented by a Declaration of Value (Dichiarazione di Valore, issued by the Italian Embassy/Consulate) OR by a CIMEA Statement of Comparability together with a Statement of Verification. The University brochure adds that holders of EHEA/Bologna-Process qualifications submit a Diploma Supplement plus a CIMEA Statement of Verification, and that holders of qualifications from Lisbon Recognition Convention signatory countries may use the CIMEA ARDI automatic-recognition platform. Per the FAQ, "EU Students just need their bachelor and transcript to be released in English from their home University and do not need a DoV."

F) SHORTFALL REMEDY — applicants who do not meet the curricular minimum are not simply rejected. The FAQ states: "In case your current bachelor does not meet the program's minimum requirement you will be able to follow individual courses to integrate your knowledge before enrolling in the program. It will be possible for you to fulfill the required 30 CFU of basic biology directly at the University of Naples paying an extra fee or to take the exams back home at your alma mater." Enrolment in single courses (corsi singoli) costs EUR 180 per the 2026/27 fee guide. Warning in the FAQ: "if you do not have ANY training in biology you do not meet the admission criteria!"

G) HOLDERS OF A HIGHER DEGREE — explicitly allowed: "A Bachelor is required but any degree above the bachelor does not prevent you from enrolling in the program." (Note that already holding a degree of the same type removes entitlement to the discounted first-year contribution — see tuition_or_fees_link.)

H) TIMING — "In any case, the required skills must be possessed before registration" (Art. 4). The University fee guide adds a general rule for master's programmes: candidates enrolling after 31 December 2026 may be required by the CCD to first acquire between 6 and 12 CFU via single courses.

No entrance examination, no portfolio and no motivation letter are required (a motivation letter and reference letters are listed only as optional "additional qualifications" for the Universitaly upload).
entry_exam_or_test:
NO entrance examination of any kind. There is no written admission test, no TOLC, no CEnT, no SAT, no national test, no portfolio and no ranking algorithm — the programme is open access and admission is decided by DOCUMENT REVIEW, with an ORAL/INTERVIEW component used only in specific cases.

1) DOCUMENT-BASED ASSESSMENT (the standard route, all nationalities). The Program Admission Committee (Commissione di Ammissione) evaluates the bachelor degree and Transcript of Records against the curricular requirements of Art. 4 of the Didactic Regulation. FAQ-1: "The Program Admission Committee for the Master's Degree program BExE will evaluate your Bachelor and transcripts, which need to be attached to your application, and will provide feedback and eventually admit you to the program." A positive outcome produces the Pre-Acceptance Letter. Art. 5 of the Didactic Regulation makes the underlying check compulsory: "Verification of personal preparation is mandatory in any case, and only students in possession of the curricular requirements can access it. The verification methods will be redefined annually by the CCD and published on the WEB site of the Department of Biology."

2) ENGLISH TEST OR INTERVIEW (conditional, not universal). Required only where an internationally recognised B2 certificate is absent or where the Committee wants confirmation:
   - CLA English test: "If you do not have a B2 English certificate or cannot prove a B2 equivalent level by other means, the Center for Language Services of the University (CLA) will organize an English Test in early September." Holding a B2 certificate exempts the candidate.
   - English interview: Art. 4 of the Didactic Regulation allows verification "through an interview, the methods of which will be indicated from time to time by the CCD". FAQ-1 warns applicants with a non-standard bachelor and transfer applicants: "You might be required to take an English Interview before being accepted."
   - A standing Department notice, "English certification: Placement Test", extends the same mechanism to matriculated first-year students who still lack a B2 certificate.
   - The Department page describes the fallback as "a placement test supported by teachers of the course".

3) NO OFA-STYLE REMEDIAL OBLIGATION IS PUBLISHED. Unlike the Department's bachelor programme, no Additional Learning Requirement (OFA) mechanism, score threshold or post-enrolment corrective exam is defined for this master's. Instead, applicants short of the curricular CFU must make them up BEFORE enrolling, by taking single courses (corsi singoli, EUR 180 each) at Federico II or equivalent exams at their home university. Separately, the University fee guide allows a CCD to require 6–12 CFU of anyone enrolling in a master's after 31 December 2026.

4) MANDATORY POST-ENROLMENT COURSE (not an admission test): a 12-hour safety course is required before joining laboratory and fieldwork activities.
language_requirements:
ENGLISH — minimum CEFR B2. This is the only compulsory language requirement.

Art. 4 of the Didactic Regulation 2025/26 (binding wording): "The course is taught in English, so the student must have adequate knowledge of it (minimum level B2 required). The verification of knowledge of the English language consists in the presentation by the student of an internationally recognized B2 level certificate or through an interview, the methods of which will be indicated from time to time by the CCD."

Two alternative ways to satisfy it:
  1) An internationally recognised B2 (or higher) English certificate. The Department page: "The graduate program can enroll students holding a certificate of proficiency in English internationally recognized. The minimum score is recognized equal to B2."
  2) If no certificate is available — a placement test / interview organised by the University Language Centre (CLA, Centro Linguistico di Ateneo) or by the programme's teachers. The FAQ states: "If you do not have a B2 English certificate or cannot prove a B2 equivalent level by other means, the Center for Language Services of the University (CLA) will organize an English Test in early September. In case you have an English language certificate or other documents supporting your knowledge of English (to a B2 level) you will not be required to take the test. Keep your application process going even if you don't have an English certificate yet!" The Department page phrases the fallback as "a placement test supported by teachers of the course".

Important practical consequence: a missing English certificate does NOT block the application. Applicants may complete the ADMISSION step without one, and the Pre-Acceptance Letter may still be issued. Applicants may, however, be called to an English interview — the FAQ warns transfer applicants and applicants with a non-standard bachelor: "You might be required to take an English Interview before being accepted."

[uncertain] NO numeric thresholds are published on any unina.it page for this programme — no IELTS band, no TOEFL score, no named list of accepted certifying bodies (unlike the Department's bachelor programme Biology for One-Health, which lists Cambridge, BEC, Trinity, IELTS and TOEFL). Equivalence to B2 is judged case by case.

A standing Department notice "English certification: Placement Test" confirms the arrangement continues after matriculation: "Students regularly enrolled in the first year who do not have a B2 level English language certification…" are directed to the placement test.

ITALIAN — NOT required for admission and not tested. The UniversItaly 2026/27 brochure applies the B2 Italian rule only to Italian-taught programmes: "For programmes taught in Italian, students must demonstrate a B2 level (CEFR)." Italian appears in this programme only as an in-course option: Year II of both curricula includes "Other activity / Italian language * (*for international student), 6 credits". Free Italian language courses are referenced in the programme FAQ under "Italian Language Courses".
application_deadline_eu:
[uncertain] A.Y. 2026/2027 — Italian and EU citizens (and non-EU citizens legally resident in Italy). Because the programme is open access there is no competition deadline; what applies are (a) an informal programme-level admission window and (b) the University's statutory enrolment calendar. Official sources give three different closing dates and are not reconciled.

PROGRAMME LEVEL (Department of Biology, "ENROLL HERE!" notice, page last modified 25/08/2026):
- Pre-enrolment opens: 1 March 2026 — "PRE-ENROLLMENT STARTING MARCH 1st! The enrollment procedure for Italian, European and International perspective students is now open!"
- Italian and EU students: "can enroll until October 31st" → 2026-10-31.
- The Department urges early action: "we suggest that you enroll as soon as possible to be able to follow the class and laboratory activities planned by the different courses!" The FAQ adds that full enrolment (fees paid, registration completed) plus a mandatory 12-hour safety course is needed to join laboratory and fieldwork activities, and recommends completing everything "by the end of September", classes starting "in the last week of September".
- The ADMISSION step (Google Form) carries no published deadline of its own for EU/Italian applicants.

UNIVERSITY LEVEL (Guida all'iscrizione A.A. 2026/27, the authoritative fee/enrolment calendar):
- Ordinary enrolment period: from 16 July 2026 ("immatricolazioni L o iscrizioni I anno LM") or from 1 September 2026, and by 2 NOVEMBER 2026 — i.e. two days later than the Department's 31 October.
- Extraordinary (late) period opens 3 November 2026.
- 15 January 2027: last date to enrol late with a EUR 50 surcharge.
- From 16 January 2027: late enrolment with a EUR 110 surcharge.
- 31 MARCH 2027: the true statutory outer limit for FIRST-YEAR master's enrolment — "Le iscrizioni al primo anno dei corsi di laurea magistrali potranno essere effettuate entro il 31 marzo 2027." Candidates enrolling after 31 December 2026 may be required by the CCD to first obtain between 6 and 12 CFU through single courses.
- Transfers into the programme (from another Federico II course or another university) run 1 September – 2 November 2026 in the ordinary period; the FAQ says transfers can be applied for online until 31 March 2027 with a late fee, and after 15 May 2027 only in person at the Segreteria.

The programme FAQ corroborates the flexible tail: "It is possible to enroll after the deadline (31st October) for Italins [sic] and EU students, paying a late fee. After March 31st, it is no longer possible to register online and therefore you will need to contact the secretariat desk." It also notes that Italian students graduating in January/February can enrol by 31 March without a late fee ("subject to confirmation by the University").

PRACTICAL READING: treat 2026-10-31 as the programme's stated deadline and 2026-11-02 as the University's ordinary deadline; enrolment remains possible with surcharges up to 2027-03-31. As of the retrieval date 2026-08-30 this window is OPEN.

Platform: SegrePass — https://www.segrepass1.unina.it/Welcome.do (or www.segrepass.unina.it).
application_deadline_non_eu:
[uncertain] A.Y. 2026/2027 — non-EU citizens resident abroad (visa-requiring applicants). Official unina.it sources disagree on the single most important date, so both readings are recorded.

STEP 0 — ADMISSION (programme level): submit the Google Form + Form 1 to the Program Admission Committee and obtain the Pre-Acceptance Letter. No published deadline of its own, but it must precede Universitaly. The University brochure advises: "It is advisable to obtain the admission to your chosen programme before applying on Universitaly. Otherwise… a dedicated team will forward your documents for evaluation. In this case, processing times may be longer."

STEP 1 — UNIVERSITALY PRE-ENROLMENT. CONFLICT:
- 2026-06-15 per the University-wide brochure "UniversItaly 2026/2027 — Information for NON-EU Students with residency abroad" and per the Department of Biology's own "ENROLL HERE!" notice ("The Universitaly deadline for Extra-European Students application is June 15th"). The brochure adds a decisive rider: "After this date no programme changes are permitted. After this date pre-enrolment is allowed to the programmes with restricted access only." Because Biology of Extreme Environments is an OPEN-ACCESS programme, this rider makes 15 June 2026 a HARD cut-off for it — the opposite of the Department's restricted-access bachelor (Biology for One-Health), for which late pre-enrolment stays open.
- 2026-07-10 per the programme's own FAQ-1 (published May 2026): "The deadline for registering and submitting your enrollment request on the Universitaly portal is July 10th, 2026. Requests arriving after this date will not be considered."
The safe assumption is 2026-06-15, since the University-wide brochure governs the Universitaly portal and the Department's public notice repeats that date.

STEP 2 — PROGRAMME ENROLMENT DEADLINE FOR EXTRA-EU: 2026-07-10 — "Extra-EU International Students have until July 10th to enroll" (Department "ENROLL HERE!" notice). The FAQ-2 calls it "a hard deadline on July 10th" (its text still says "2023", a stale year).

STEP 3 — VISA: 2026-11-30 — "Deadline for submitting the visa application at Italian Embassies/Consulates".

STEP 4 — MATRICULATION / FINAL ENROLMENT IN NAPLES: 2027-01-31 — "Deadline for completing enrolment at University of Naples Federico II. After this date students who are not officially enrolled according to ministerial regulations will have their visa revoked, and Italian police authorities will be notified." ([uncertain] page 8 of the same brochure mis-prints this as "by 31 January 2026"; the Deadlines page and the surrounding 2026/27 calendar make 31 January 2027 the correct reading.)

STEP 5 — RESIDENCE PERMIT: apply within 8 days of arrival in Italy.

As of the retrieval date 2026-08-30, the non-EU Universitaly and programme-enrolment windows for 2026/27 have CLOSED; only the visa (30 Nov 2026) and final-enrolment (31 Jan 2027) stages remain open for candidates already pre-enrolled. Prospective 2027/28 applicants should expect the same pattern (pre-enrolment from 1 March, Universitaly by mid-June, programme enrolment by 10 July) but the 2027/28 dates were not published as of the retrieval date.

Contacts for confirmation: bioextreme@unina.it (programme), pre-enrolment@unina.it (University pre-enrolment office — include programme name and pre-application number in the subject line), international@unina.it.
required_documents:
A) ADMISSION STEP — uploaded as a SINGLE PDF to the online form https://forms.gle/6DNRdeKQ4m5FQEkUA (required of all applicants; EU/Italian holders of L-13, L-32 or L-2 bachelors may skip straight to enrolment):
- Bachelor Diploma
- Transcript of Records (ToR) in English, with a detailed description of the courses attended and the exams passed to obtain the final degree (only for foreign students)
- Copy of the passport (only for foreign students)
- An updated CV
- Certificate of English language (when available/necessary — not blocking if absent)
- Other relevant documents
- Plus, downloaded, completed, signed and re-uploaded: "FORM 1 – Recognition of Foreign University Title" (https://drive.google.com/file/d/12hlNFzHTCPyfK_8H_jRYN3dZIiUeTFdj)
Output of this step: the PRE-ACCEPTANCE LETTER issued by the Programme Coordinator.

B) EXTRA-EU — UNIVERSITALY PRE-ENROLMENT UPLOAD (PDF/JPEG/PNG, max 10 MB each):
- Passport-size photograph of the face only
- Valid passport
- Final degree certificate or Diploma
- Transcript of Records (ToR) with detailed course descriptions
- Pre-acceptance letter from the Programme Coordinator
- A copy of Form 1 – Recognition of foreign university title
- Additional qualifications: language certificates, motivation letter, letters of recommendation
- Declaration of Value (DoV) issued by the Italian Embassy/Consulate, OR CIMEA Statement of Comparability together with Statement of Verification (EHEA/Bologna-Process qualifications: Diploma Supplement + CIMEA Statement of Verification; Lisbon Convention signatory countries may use the CIMEA ARDI platform)
- Selection of the Embassy/Consulate where the visa will be requested, and of the academic programme (curriculum choice optional at this stage)
The University brochure's master's-level list adds "Detailed course descriptions" as a separate required item.

C) EXTRA-EU — FINAL ENROLMENT IN NAPLES (at the Student Office / International Office, international@unina.it):
- All the above documents in original/certified form
- Italian tax code (codice fiscale) — mandatory for enrolment, obtainable from the Agenzia delle Entrate or an Italian embassy
- Valid visa and, after arrival, the residence permit application (within 8 days of arrival)
- Proof of payment of the university fees
- Proof of health insurance coverage (non-EU citizens must show proof of health insurance; EU citizens use the European Health Insurance Card)

D) ITALIAN AND EU STUDENTS — ENROLMENT VIA SEGREPASS:
- Registration on SegrePass (https://www.segrepass1.unina.it/Welcome.do), then the online enrolment procedure
- ISEEU declaration data (retrieved automatically from the INPS database at enrolment; students who do not provide ISEEU data pay the maximum contribution). The ISEE is obtained via a CAF or an INPS office by filing the DSU.
- Proof of English proficiency / completion of the Admission form
- EU students: bachelor degree and transcript issued in English by the home university (no Declaration of Value needed), plus a codice fiscale obtainable through the International Welcome Desk
- Payment of the first instalment plus regional tax and stamp duty
- The FAQ specifies the paper follow-up: documentation must be delivered to the Student Office "Within 10 days from the ID number (matricola) reception."

E) TRANSFER APPLICANTS (from another Italian university): Admission form first; then the incoming-transfer request form from https://www.unina.it/modulistica/segreteria-studenti, payment of the previous-career transcription fee, payment of the first instalment and regional tax, submission of the ISEE model, and delivery of all documentation to the Secretariat — all within the ordinary enrolment terms.
tuition_or_fees_link:
[uncertain] Official fees hub: https://www.unina.it/it/didattica/iscrizioni-e-tasse (English: https://www.unina.it/en/didattica/iscrizioni-e-tasse). Fee simulator/calculator: http://calcolatrice.unina.it. Authoritative 2026/27 document: "Guida all'iscrizione A.A. 2026-27" — https://www.unina.it/documents/d/guest/guida_studente_rapida_26-27_10-7-2026 (also indexed at https://www.unina.it/didattica/sportello-studenti/guide-dello-studente).

A.Y. 2026/2027 SUMMARY (university-wide; there is no programme-specific surcharge for Biology of Extreme Environments). The contribution is income- and career-based, calculated on the ISEEU (university ISEE) and CFU earned.
- FIRST-YEAR ENROLMENT (which is what a new master's student pays): the "contributo agevolato" (reduced contribution) applies — EXEMPT if ISEEU up to EUR 30,000; otherwise a fixed EUR 1,011.50 plus a variable component according to ISEEU, up to a maximum of EUR 2,384.00 for those who file no ISEEU declaration. The guide states explicitly that a bachelor graduate enrolling for the first time in year 1 of a two-year master's is entitled to the reduced contribution.
- Above EUR 80,000 of ISEEU the amounts are no longer differentiated by income.
- MASTER'S-SPECIFIC DISCOUNT: 50% reduction of the contribution for a student enrolling in year 1 of a master's who obtained the three-year bachelor by October of the final year (third year, in corso) with a grade of 110 cum laude.
- CAVEAT: the reduced first-year contribution can be used only ONCE. Applicants who previously withdrew from or forfeited a university career, or who already hold a degree of the same type as the one they are enrolling in, must pay the ordinary contribution for year 1 (with a 10% reduction if ISEEU is within the NO TAX area of EUR 30,000). This is directly relevant here because the programme explicitly admits applicants who already hold a master's degree.
- REGIONAL TAX for the right to study, in three ISEEU bands: EUR 130.00 (ISEEU up to EUR 25,500, and students from particularly poor countries under Art. 13(5) DPCM 9 April 2001 / D.M. 176 of 24 February 2026); EUR 151.00 (ISEEU between EUR 25,500.01 and EUR 51,000, AND students whose family unit resides abroad — the band most international students fall into); EUR 173.00 (ISEEU above EUR 51,000 and those filing no ISEEU).
- STAMP DUTY (imposta di bollo): EUR 16.00.
- INSTALMENTS: 1st instalment = 60% of the amount + regional tax + stamp duty, payable from 16 July 2026 (or from 1 September) and by 2 November 2026; 2nd instalment = 20% by 1 March 2027; 3rd instalment = 20% by 30 April 2027. A EUR 100 surcharge applies from 16 July 2027 to students who did not pay the 2nd or 3rd instalment.
- LATE-ENROLMENT SURCHARGES: EUR 50 up to 15 January 2027; EUR 110 from 16 January 2027.
- OTHER CHARGES relevant to this programme: single-course enrolment (used to make up missing CFU) EUR 180; transfer in/out or previous-career transcription EUR 96; career suspension EUR 202; duplicate parchment EUR 52.

CONFLICTING (APPARENTLY STALE) FIGURES: the programme's own FAQ-1 and the international.unina.it "Admission regulation" page both quote a much simpler and far lower schedule — "EU students EUR 200/year (university fees) + EUR 140/year regional tax (compulsory) + EUR 16.00 legal stamp (compulsory)" and "Non EU students EUR 140/year regional tax (compulsory) + EUR 16.00 legal stamp (compulsory)". These are irreconcilable with the 2026/27 guide (regional tax 130/151/173; ISEEU-based contribution) and should be treated as outdated. Use the 2026/27 guide and calcolatrice.unina.it. Italian citizens who omit ISEEU data pay the maximum fees.

seats_total: [uncertain] NOT PUBLISHED — no capped intake exists. The programme is open access: the orientamento.unina.it course card states "Admission Libero", and no numero programmato, no total number of places and no ranking list are published on any unina.it page. Art. 5 of the Didactic Regulation reserves to the CCD the "possible planning of enrolments" but no such planning has been enacted or published. Intake is therefore limited only by the curricular and English requirements screened by the Program Admission Committee.
non_eu_reserved_seats: [uncertain] NOT PUBLISHED — no reserved contingent (contingente riservato ai cittadini non comunitari residenti all'estero) is published for this programme on any unina.it page. Federico II publishes such per-programme quotas only for restricted-access (numero programmato) degrees; for open-access programmes such as this one, non-EU applicants resident abroad are admitted on the strength of the Programme Coordinator's Pre-Acceptance Letter and the Universitaly pre-enrolment procedure rather than against a numeric quota. The international.unina.it admission regulation makes no mention of quotas for open-access programmes. Prospective applicants should confirm with pre-enrolment@unina.it, since the ministerial contingent tables are normally settled in April–May and published on the MUR website.

uncertainty_notes:
1) NON-EU UNIVERSITALY DEADLINE CONFLICT (most consequential). The Department of Biology's own notice and the University-wide UniversItaly 2026/27 brochure both give 15 June 2026 as the Universitaly pre-enrolment deadline, while the programme's FAQ-1 (published May 2026) states 10 July 2026 for the same portal step. The brochure additionally rules that after 15 June pre-enrolment continues "to the programmes with restricted access only" — and this programme is OPEN access, which makes 15 June a hard stop for it. The most coherent reading is: Universitaly by 15 June 2026, programme-side enrolment completion by 10 July 2026. Applicants must confirm with pre-enrolment@unina.it and bioextreme@unina.it. Note this is the OPPOSITE of the same Department's restricted-access bachelor (Biology for One-Health), where late non-EU pre-enrolment remains possible.

2) EU/ITALIAN CLOSING DATE CONFLICT. The Department page says Italian and EU students "can enroll until October 31st"; the University's Guida all'iscrizione 2026/27 sets the ordinary period end at 2 November 2026; and § 6 of the same guide allows first-year master's enrolment up to 31 March 2027 (with EUR 50 / EUR 110 late surcharges and a possible 6–12 CFU precondition after 31 December 2026). All three are simultaneously true at different levels of authority; 31 October is the programme's advisory date, 2 November the statutory ordinary deadline, 31 March 2027 the outer limit.

3) CONFLICTING CURRICULAR REQUIREMENT TABLES. Art. 4 of the Didactic Regulation (and the orientamento and scuolapsb pages, which copy it) requires roughly 30 CFU BIO/* + MED/04 + MED/42, 6 CFU maths/informatics, 6 CFU physics, 6 CFU chemistry. The programme FAQ-1 imposes a heavier 60-CFU distribution over six SSD groups plus a 90-CFU minimum bachelor. These are not reconciled anywhere on unina.it. The Didactic Regulation is the binding instrument; the FAQ likely reflects the Admission Committee's working practice. Borderline applicants should have the Committee assess them explicitly.

4) STALE YEARS INSIDE THE 2026/27 FAQ. FAQ-1 is dated "Last update May 15" and was published in May 2026, but retains uncorrected text from earlier cycles: "will close on October 31st 2023", "select the academic year (the upcoming one is 2023/2024)", and FAQ-2's "Extra-EU Students have a hard deadline on July 10th 2023". The 2026 dates that do appear ("July 10th, 2026") were updated; the surrounding text was not. Treat year references inside the FAQs with caution.

5) TYPO IN THE UNIVERSITALY BROCHURE. The "Deadlines" page correctly gives JAN 31 2027 as the enrolment-completion deadline, but the "Matriculation" page of the same document says "students who obtained visa are required to matriculate by 31 January 2026". 31 January 2027 is the correct date for A.Y. 2026/2027.

6) ADMISSION-STEP SCOPE AMBIGUITY. The orientamento card and the Department page both describe the ADMISSION procedure (Google Form + FORM 1) as "common to ALL the students (Italian, EU and Extra-EU)" and "mandatory", yet the Department page's EU/Italian section says holders of an L-13, L-32 or L-2 bachelor "may proceed directly to the Enrollment procedure". FAQ-1 partly resolves it: Italian students follow the standard online procedure with "The only additional step ... the requirement to fill in the Admission form ... and provide proof of English proficiency." Safest reading: everyone should submit the Admission form; only the Committee's academic-evaluation step is waived for L-13/L-32/L-2 holders.

7) NO SEAT NUMBERS EXIST. seats_total and non_eu_reserved_seats are marked uncertain because they are genuinely NOT published, not because sources conflict — the programme is open access with no numero programmato and no non-EU contingent published on any unina.it page. Federico II publishes per-programme non-EU quotas only for restricted-access degrees.

8) TUITION FIGURES CONFLICT. The programme FAQ and international.unina.it both publish a flat "EUR 200/year + EUR 140 regional tax + EUR 16 stamp" (EU) / "EUR 140 + EUR 16" (non-EU) schedule that is irreconcilable with the 2026/27 Guida all'iscrizione (ISEEU-based contribution, exempt up to EUR 30,000, max EUR 2,384.00; regional tax 130/151/173). The flat figures appear stale; the 2026/27 guide and calcolatrice.unina.it are authoritative. Also note the first-year discount is forfeited by applicants who already hold a degree of the same type — directly relevant since the programme explicitly welcomes applicants who already hold a master's.

9) NO NUMERIC ENGLISH THRESHOLDS. Unlike some other Federico II programmes, no IELTS/TOEFL score bands and no list of accepted certifying bodies are published for this programme — only "internationally recognized B2" plus a CLA placement test / CCD interview fallback.

10) DATA CURRENCY AND PAGE STATE. Department of Biology pages were last modified 25/08/2026; the FAQ PDFs were published 22 May 2026; the fee guide is dated 10/07/2026. Retrieved 2026-08-30. The orientamento.unina.it course card is visibly older in places — its "Graduation dates" section still lists Academic Year 2023/2024 sessions. As of the retrieval date the EU/Italian enrolment window for 2026/27 is OPEN, while the non-EU Universitaly and programme-enrolment windows have CLOSED.

11) TLS AND CONTENT-INTEGRITY CAVEATS. The orientamento.unina.it host presents a TLS chain that some fetchers reject ("unable to verify the first certificate"); the page was retrieved successfully but certificate warnings should be expected. Separately, the Department of Biology WordPress site carries injected SEO spam text in its page footers; this was ignored and had no bearing on any extracted fact.

12) OFF-DOMAIN SOURCES DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED. The programme also runs a self-hosted site at bioextreme.it, and its application forms are Google-hosted (forms.gle / drive.google.com). Per the source restriction, no fact in this record is sourced from bioextreme.it. The Google-hosted admission form and FORM 1 are cited only because they are the application entry points linked directly from the official unina.it pages; the FAQ PDFs, by contrast, are hosted on the unina.it domain and are treated as official.

13) DIPLOMA NAME. The awarded Italian degree title is "Biologia degli Ambienti Estremi" (class LM-6 Biologia); the English designation "Biology of Extreme Environments" is used throughout. There is no divergence between programme name and diploma name beyond the language of record. Graduates are trained as Biologists with access to research, space-agency and biotechnology careers.
